title: Walk & Talk Cornwall Park: Conversations that Matter
location: Green Lane West, Epsom, Auckland 1051, New Zealand, Auckland
description:
Sick of loud bars, awkward small talk, and surface-level chats?
I am too.

Let’s do something low-key - but *real*.

**🌿 Walk & Talk** \- a casual\, open\-invite stroll with people who enjoy movement\, connection\, and actual conversation\.

No agenda, no pressure, and no hierarchies.

Just walking. Talking. Sharing thoughts. Or simply listening. Flat surface - energy spent on the talk, not the terrain.

Bring your water bottle & hat. Also bring your thoughts, your awkwardness - it’s all welcome.

The event language is English, but you are welcome to use other languages when chatting with others.

📅 **Date & Time:** Sunday, November 1, 5 pm
**📍 Meeting Spot:** Entrance to Cornwall Park Cafe
**🚶‍♂️ Route:** Cornwall Park Loop Path
**🐢 Pace:** Chill
**💬 Vibe:** Honest, warm, thoughtful

Drop me a message if you’re curious - or just show up 🙂

In case of difficulty finding the group, check the live location - it will be posted when the walk starts!

If you want to share your ride coming to the event, write so in the comments!

**Walk & Talk walks are free.** Optional koha: [https://www.walkandtalk.org.nz/#koha](https://www.walkandtalk.org.nz/#koha). Payment details are never posted on Meetup, so please ignore any you see here.

title: JuniorDev Auckland Meet
location: 125 The Strand, Parnell, Auckland 1010, New Zealand, Auckland
description:
We’re happy to announce the next **JuniorDev Auckland event**!

Join us for an evening of learning and connection as we hear from our speakers and the experiences they’ll be sharing.

**Important Note for Attendees:**

* **Please note of the new location for the event: [Directions to Serko House](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1M8Jt_-5DmBABSiNnaDpCpNiHNfxMRCICI1eRBjne-08/edit?tab=t.0) (Just 2 mins away from Xero)**

**Talk 1: Finding Joy After AI: An Inside Out Look at How We Work by Kevin Meneses**
Inspired by Disney and Pixar's Inside Out films, this (pre-recorded) talk uses their premise as a framework to explore what team survey data reveals about AI adoption, productivity, and working hours, offering practical ways to thrive in an AI-assisted workflow.

**A bit about Kevin:**

* Kevin is a Junior Software Engineer at Fergus who transitioned into engineering from the Customer Support team after completing a full stack developer programme.

**Talk 2: Building AI without Losing Our Values by**
**Lauren Peate**
AI is here to stay – hype, copyright theft, data worker mistreatment, environmental harm, and all. If you care about people and the planet but also need to understand new tech, what can you do? I’ll recommend a middle ground – using AI in features and workflows without compromising our values. Combining my own experience with insights from our original research with hundreds of global developers, I’ll share examples of how to use this tech with care.

**A bit about Lauren:**

* Lauren Peate is a data nerd who cares about people. She’s founder and CEO of Multitudes, which turns engineering metrics into a tool for continuous improvement – in AI, engineering productivity, developer experience, and more. Through her career, she’s worked with a wide range of organizations, from Fortune 500 tech companies in San Francisco to startups in the Middle East. Previously on a PhD track, she started her career conducting independent research through a Fulbright grant.

title: Level Up; Q&A with CODE's Tim Ponting
description:
Time to level up! This month we are excited to host Tim Ponting, Chief Executive of the New Zealand Centre of Digital Excellence (CODE), a government-funded economic development initiative tasked with helping build a sustainable game development ecosystem in Aotearoa.

Tim will give a brief update about CODE’s present activities and future plans, before opening the floor to any questions about CODE and its operations.

**About Tim**
Tim Ponting is a video game industry veteran with over 35 years’ experience working in a variety of roles, initially as editor and publisher of magazines and websites and then in marketing communications roles, including 5 years as European PR Director for Activision and over 15 years as director of a communications and business development agency Renegade. He has been a serial investor in video game projects and studios here in Aotearoa since 2018.

title: Welcome to the next AWS Auckland Well-Architected Meetup for 2026!
location: Level 13, Commercial Bay, 15 Customs Street West, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1010, Auckland
description:
Hi Architects,

Welcome to the next AWS Auckland Well Architected User Group Meetup of 2026!

At each meetup, we focus on learning and networking in a friendly and inclusive atmosphere and explore best-practices in AWS. This has resulted in the AWS Well-Architected Meetups becoming the most popular AWS Meetups in ANZ 🥳

**Please also note that AWS Security now requests a company name and company email where it is available. If you are a student, please list your institution and your student email address at that institution 👍**

We'll be announcing more speakers on [https://well-architected.me](https://well-architected.me/) and previewing presentations during the coming weeks - our speakers and details this month include:

* **Michael Taylor, Lakebase Specialist, Databricks**

**How Lakebase provides a well-architected platform for next generation application and AI development.**
Come and hear how Databricks experts show how customers run applications and agents on Lakebase; serverless Postgres governed by Unity Catalog. See instant branching, scale-to-zero, point-in-time recovery and synced tables in action. The Databricks team will also give a first look at LTAP; one open, governed copy of data for transactions and analytics, with no ETL in between.

* **Kristof Ringleff, Solution Architect, Fooman**

**From Weekend Project to Well-Architected: Putting AWS's new Well-Architected Agent to Work**

Kristoff had a small serverless weekend project running on AWS. So he pointed the brand-new AWS Well-Architected Agent at it. Then I did what any sensible engineer would do with a hobby app; I followed its advice. This talk covers what the agent found, what I learned along the way and the fun of over-engineering something that never needed it. I'll also compare it with the open-source Well-Architected Review skill, which runs in your own coding agent and needs no AWS Support plan.

* **Mystery Speaker**

**The AWS AI Competency - can automation support?**
Achieving the AW
